etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English feithful, equivalent to faith +‎ -ful.

definitions.definition: Loyal; adhering firmly to person or cause.

My dog is very faithful: he doesn't like to be petted by anybody else.

quote.citation: 2009, Paul Lakeland, Church: Living Communion, page 162:
quote.text: The application of the old discipline, say the conservatives, would probably produce a smaller but more faithful Church.

definitions.definition: Engaging in sexual relations only with one's spouse or long-term sexual partner.

quote.text: She wanted to be free to explore casual affairs, but her man had to be faithful.

definitions.definition: (mathematics) Injective in specific contexts, e.g. of representations in representation or functors in category theory.
(ring theory, of a module) Whose annihilator is zero.
(in the plural) The practicing members of a religion or followers of a cause.

quote.citation: 1984, 2:11:25 from the start, in Dune‎[1] (Science Fiction), spoken by Paul Atreides, →OCLC:
quote.text: We Fremen have a saying: God created Arrakis to train the faithful. One cannot go against the word of God.

definitions.definition: Someone or something that is faithful or reliable.

quote.citation: 2009 September 30, Bruce DeMara, “Shaw's comedy gets teeth”, in Toronto Star‎[2]:
quote.text: Earlier this year, as the recession put a damper on ticket sales, Maxwell said the easy route would have been to go for the tried-and-true old faithfuls.
